findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default JCE provider, not BouncyCastle
findings.body: The implementation calls `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which returns the provider of the JVM's default keystore type (typically SUN for JKS or SunJSSE for PKCS12), not BouncyCastle. The interface contract in CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider documents that it must return a BouncyCastle security provider (non-FIPS or FIPS). When this provider is selected by CryptoIntegration (which happens whenever authz-client is used standalone, since DefaultCryptoProvider is not on that classpath), any caller that does `Signature.getInstance(alg, prov)` or similar expecting BC will silently get a different provider. That breaks the contract and can cause ECDSA verification to fall back to SunEC/SUN (or fail outright if BC is required for the curve/algorithm), defeating the purpose of this class for the standalone 3rd-party use case.

findings.title: Test only verifies round-trip consistency, not correctness against a reference
findings.body: The test asserts `rsConcat2 == rsConcat` after running `sign -> asn1derToConcatenatedRS -> concatenatedRSToASN1DER -> asn1derToConcatenatedRS`. This is an idempotency property test, not a correctness test: if both converters are biased the same way (e.g., they swap r and s, off-by-one the padding, or always strip the leading zero byte) the round-trip still matches and the assertion passes. The test never checks that the produced `rsConcat` actually equals the raw r||s bytes that the JDK signature produced, nor compares against BouncyCastle's BCECDSACryptoProvider output. A reference comparison (or parsing the original DER signature with java.security and comparing the integers byte-for-byte) is needed to actually validate the conversion.

findings.title: Two ASN1Encoder instances are created and discarded on every call to concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` and throw away the returned encoders. They have no effect on the result (the real encoding is produced by the two encoders passed into `writeDerSeq` on lines 119-120). These are dead allocations executed on every signature verification; they should be removed.
